title: Unresponsive Person / Cardiac Arrest
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020; American Heart Association (AHA) Guidelines for CPR and ECC 2020

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately and place phone on speaker beside the patient
Check response and breathing: gently tap shoulders and shout loudly; look for normal chest rise for no more than 10 seconds
If unresponsive and not breathing normally, place patient on a firm, flat surface
Position heel of one hand in the center of the chest (lower half of breastbone), place other hand on top and interlock fingers
Deliver hard and fast chest compressions: 5 to 6 cm deep at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute
Allow complete chest recoil between compressions; do not interrupt compressions unless an AED is ready or patient begins breathing normally
If an AED arrives, turn it on immediately and follow the automated voice prompts

do_not: Do not leave the person unattended unless absolutely necessary to call for help
Do not place a pillow or support under the person's head
Do not attempt to give water, food, or oral medications to an unconscious person
Do not slap, shake vigorously, or throw water on the face
